goal: Migrate the five public Ledger operations to the existing Effect runtime while preserving legacy Currency consumers until step 03.

tasks.name: Add Ledger domain, error, and transport contracts
inputs: Approved Ledgers Effect design
Ledger terminology and invariants from CONTEXT.md
Existing LedgerID and OrgID branded types
Existing TypeBox and RFC 7807-compatible error conventions
tasks.description: Create a Currency-free immutable Ledger domain value and a LedgerWrite value for persistence commands. Add Ledger-specific not-found, dependency, repository-unavailable, decoding, and persistence errors while reusing the public OrganizationNotFound error for a missing parent. Define TypeBox schemas for canonical Ledger IDs, offset pagination capped at 10,000, create and update bodies with additionalProperties false, and Currency-free responses. Add the response mapper with ISO timestamps and omission of absent optional fields. The domain must not import Effect, Fastify, TypeBox, Drizzle, database rows, or environment code.

tests: Type-check the API package after adding the contracts
acceptance: Ledger and LedgerWrite contain no Currency or Minor Unit Exponent
Metadata accepts only string values
List offset defaults to 0 with a maximum of 10,000, and limit defaults to 20 with a maximum of 100
Create and update schemas remove undeclared input under the existing Fastify AJV configuration
Response mapping emits ISO timestamps and omits absent description and metadata

tasks.name: Implement repository reads and persisted-row decoding
inputs: Ledger domain and error contracts from T1
DatabaseTag and the existing Drizzle LedgersTable
Shared parseId, PostgreSQL availability classifier, and PostgreSQL error-code classifier
Organization repository integration-test Layer pattern
tasks.description: Define LedgerRepo, LedgerRepoTag, LedgerRepoLive, and the repository Layer. Add a private decoder for Ledger and Organization IDs, UTC timestamps, JSON object shape, and string-valued metadata. Implement tenant-scoped list and get queries that select only public columns. Order lists by Ledger ID ascending, apply offset and limit in PostgreSQL, and return Option.none for a missing or cross-Organization get. Map unavailable queries to LedgerRepositoryUnavailable, decoding failures to LedgerPersistenceDecodingFailure, and other failures to LedgerPersistenceFailure.

tests: List results are ordered by Ledger ID and paginated in PostgreSQL
List and get enforce Organization isolation
Get returns explicit absence for missing and cross-Organization rows
Valid string-valued metadata decodes
Invalid IDs, malformed JSON, non-object JSON, and non-string metadata values produce LedgerPersistenceDecodingFailure
acceptance: Normal queries select only id, organization_id, name, description, metadata, created, and updated
Every repository read includes the Organization ID in its SQL filter
Repository failures remain in the typed Effect error channel
The focused Ledger repository test passes against PostgreSQL

tasks.name: Implement separate repository writes and compatibility checks
inputs: Ledger repository read implementation from T2
Existing database defaults for timestamps, currency, and currency_exponent
Retained legacy LedgerRepo.getLedger path
Existing Ledger Account foreign-key schema
tasks.description: Extend LedgerRepo with separate create, update, and delete operations without upsert. Create inserts only the generated ID, Organization ID, and public mutable fields so PostgreSQL supplies timestamps and legacy Currency defaults. Update filters by both IDs, replaces mutable fields, writes SQL NULL for omitted optional fields, sets updated with PostgreSQL time, and never inserts. Delete filters by both IDs and returns explicit absence. Map create 23503 to OrganizationNotFound, generated-ID 23505 to LedgerPersistenceFailure, and delete 23503 to LedgerHasDependents. Keep repository unavailability retryable at this boundary so the service can apply the create-specific policy.

tests: Duplicate Ledger names can be created
Create receives PostgreSQL timestamps and legacy USD and 2 defaults
Create with a missing Organization maps 23503 to OrganizationNotFound
A generated-ID collision maps 23505 to LedgerPersistenceFailure
Update replaces mutable fields, clears omitted optionals, preserves created, and changes updated
Update of a missing or cross-Organization Ledger returns absence and never inserts
Updating a row with non-default legacy Currency and exponent preserves both values through the retained legacy read
Delete returns absence for missing and cross-Organization rows
A real dependent Ledger Account maps delete 23503 to LedgerHasDependents
acceptance: Create, update, and delete are distinct SQL operations
No write changes currency or currency_exponent
Every update and delete includes both Ledger and Organization IDs in its SQL filter
The complete Ledger repository test passes against PostgreSQL

tasks.name: Add the Effect Ledger service
inputs: Complete LedgerRepo capability from T3
Effect 4.0.0-beta.105 Context.Service and Layer conventions
Installed typeid-js library
Existing HttpError hierarchy
tasks.description: Add LedgerService with list, get, create, update, and delete operations that receive the authenticated Organization ID explicitly. Generate canonical Ledger IDs directly with typeid-js inside Effect.sync so generation remains lazy, and construct LedgerWrite values without an ID-generator service. Forward pagination and tenant identifiers unchanged. Convert absent get, update, and delete results to LedgerNotFound. Preserve typed repository failures except during create, where LedgerRepositoryUnavailable becomes a ServiceUnavailableError with retryable false. Export concrete service error-channel types and assemble the service Layer from LedgerRepoTag.

tests: All five operations forward the Organization ID
List also forwards offset and limit
Create generates a canonical Ledger TypeID and calls only repository create
Update calls only repository update
Absent get, update, and delete results map to LedgerNotFound
Dependency and persistence failures remain typed
Create unavailability has retryable false
Unavailability from list, get, update, and delete retains retryable true
Compile-time assertions show every exported service error extends HttpError
acceptance: LedgerService is available through a Context service and Layer
Ledger ID generation remains lazy inside Effect.sync
The service contains no authentication, rate limiting, retry, or generic execution logic
The focused Ledger service test passes

tasks.name: Replace the public Ledger routes
inputs: Ledger transport schemas and response mapper from T1
LedgerServiceTag from T4
Existing managed runtime and global error handler
Current Ledger permissions and direct Organization route pattern
tasks.description: Add direct Effect handlers for GET collection, GET item, POST, PUT, and DELETE on the existing Ledger paths. Parse path IDs with parseId, run programs through the managed server runtime, convert Effect results at the HTTP boundary, and throw typed failures to the global handler. Keep existing permissions. Advertise only failures the operations produce, omitting 409 from create and update and omitting 429 from every Ledger route. Return 201 with Location for create and an empty 204 for delete. Keep Fastify's current AJV configuration so additionalProperties false removes undeclared input.

tests: The five existing permission declarations remain attached
All five handlers pass the authenticated Organization ID to the mocked service
Pagination defaults, the 10,000 maximum offset, and limit bounds are enforced
Malformed and noncanonical Ledger IDs return 400
Currency fields and arbitrary undeclared properties are stripped before POST and PUT reach the service
Missing and malformed declared fields return 400
Responses contain no Currency fields
Create returns 201 with Location and delete returns an empty 204
Not-found and dependency errors map to 404 and 409
Create-time unavailability maps to 503 with retryable false
acceptance: All five public paths and success representations match the approved design
Routes use LedgerService through the managed runtime
No Ledger route advertises 429 or a nonexistent conflict
The focused Ledger route test passes

Leave the legacy LedgerService, LedgerRepo, LedgerEntity, route schemas, RepoPlugin, and ServicePlugin intact for child-resource compatibility.
